attempts.summary: Configured node1 (SONiC) as a transit router between node2 and node3 over dedicated point-to-point links (node1 eth1 192.168.1.1/30 <-> node2 eth1 192.168.1.2/30; node1 eth2 192.168.2.1/30 <-> node3 eth1 192.168.2.2/30), enabled IPv4 forwarding, added static routes on node2/node3 via node1 for the opposite subnet, opened firewalld ports 8080/tcp and 23/tcp on node2/node3 host firewalls so the transit ACL on node1 is the sole enforcement point, and installed an nftables 'inet transit_acl' forward-hook table on node1 that rejects (TCP RST) forwarded tcp/23 in both directions while leaving all other forwarded traffic (including tcp/8080 and ICMP) untouched. All configuration was made persistent (interfaces.d stanza + sysctl.d + a transit-acl.service nftables unit on node1; NetworkManager connection profiles + firewalld --permanent on node2/node3). Verified end-to-end with real TCP listeners: 8080 connects successfully both directions, 23 is refused both directions, ICMP passes. Then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes (node1, then node2, then node3), each verified via a changed OS boot_id, and confirmed post-restart that SONiC's 9 containers were healthy, all persisted network/ACL config auto-reapplied without manual intervention, and the 8080-allowed/23-refused behavior still held in both directions.
